history.dynasty: None (natural cave shrine; some sources attribute antiquity to the Gupta era)
history.period: Ancient natural formation; exact date of worship unverified
history.summary: A natural limestone cave shrine north of Pachmarhi whose stalactites and stalagmites resemble Shiva's matted hair (jata), with 108 naturally formed lingams revered inside. Regional tradition holds that Shiva concealed himself here from the demon Bhasmasura. The cave also holds two spring-fed ponds (one cold, one warm) and an underground stream known as the Gupt Ganga.

name: Jata Shankar Cave Temple
town_description: Pachmarhi is a hill station in the Satpura Range of Madhya Pradesh, at about 1,067 m elevation, widely known as 'Satpura ki Rani' (Queen of Satpura). It has been a cantonment town since the British Raj and lies wholly within the Pachmarhi Biosphere Reserve and the Satpura Tiger Reserve. It is Madhya Pradesh's only hill station and the base for reaching sites like Dhupgarh, Chauragarh and the Jata Shankar caves.

travel.airport: Nearest airport is Bhopal, about 200-210 km away (verify)
travel.railway: Nearest railway station is Pipariya, about 47-55 km away (verify)
travel.road: About 1.5 km from the Pachmarhi bus station; accessible by road with marked paths and steps down into the ravine

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Maha Shivaratri (February-March) draws the largest crowds
